items.prompt: Match each Greek or Latin root to its meaning.
hints: Think of a word you know that contains each root.
Use the meaning of the whole word to work out what the root means.
Start with telescope. What does a telescope help you to see?
items.explanation: A telescope sees far away, biology is the study of life and geography describes the earth. A microscope shows very small things, an aquarium holds water and a portable radio can be carried.

items.prompt: Tele means far and scope means look. What is a telescope used for?

options.why: Scope is about looking, not hearing.

options.text: looking at things that are far away

options.why: That is a microscope. Micro means small.
Graph means write. Scope means look.

hints: Put the two meanings together.
Tele tells you where the things are, and scope tells you what you do.
Say it as a phrase: far plus look.
items.explanation: A telescope is used to look at things that are far away, such as planets and stars.

items.prompt: Auto means self and graph means write. Which word means a person’s own signature?

options.why: A paragraph is a group of sentences.
Photo means light. A photograph is made with light.
A biography is writing about another person’s life.

hints: Look for a word with both roots in it.
Your own signature is something you write yourself.
Split each word into its two parts, then check what each part means.
items.explanation: Autograph means self plus write: your own name, written by you.

items.prompt: The root aud means hear. Complete the word. The ___ clapped loudly at the end of the concert.
hints: The missing word names the people who listen at a concert.
It begins with the root aud.
Say it aloud: aud... What do we call a group of listeners?
items.explanation: An audience is a group of people who hear or watch a performance. The word comes from aud, meaning hear.

items.prompt: Therm means heat and meter means measure. Write the name of an instrument that measures temperature.
hints: Join the two roots together.
You need an o between the two roots to make the word easy to say.
Join the two roots with one vowel in between, then say the word aloud.
items.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is: therm (heat) + meter (measure).

items.prompt: Sort the words by the meaning of their root.
hints: Look for these roots: vis, vid, spect, aud, phon, graph and scrib.
Vis, vid and spect come from Latin words about seeing. Think about what the other roots mean.
Start with video. Do you watch it, listen to it or write it?
items.explanation: Visible, spectator and video are about seeing. Audio, microphone and auditorium are about hearing or sound. Autograph, manuscript and scribble are about writing.

items.prompt: Which English word comes from Malay words meaning person of the forest?

options.why: Gibbon came into English through French.
Gorilla comes from an old Greek word.
Chimpanzee comes from a language spoken in central Africa.

hints: The animal lives in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra.
In Malay and Indonesian, orang means person and hutan means forest.
Say each animal name aloud and listen for Malay words you know.
items.explanation: Orangutan comes from the Malay words orang (person) and hutan (forest). English has borrowed many words from other languages.

items.prompt: Rupt means break. Which word means to break into a conversation?

options.why: Erupt means to burst out, like a volcano.
A rupture is a break or tear in something, such as a pipe.
Abrupt means sudden.

hints: Look at the prefix in front of rupt in each word.
Inter means between.
Ask which word means breaking in between people who are talking.
items.explanation: Interrupt comes from inter (between) and rupt (break). When you interrupt, you break into a conversation.

items.prompt: Chron comes from the Greek word for time. Choose all the words that are about time.

options.why: Chrome comes from a Greek word for colour.
Chorus comes from a Greek word for a group of singers and dancers.

hints: Look for the letters chron in each word.
Words that look alike can come from different roots.
Check each word: does it mean something to do with time?
items.explanation: Chronological means in time order, a chronicle is a record of events over time and synchronise means make things happen at the same time.

items.prompt: Which pair of words share a root with the same meaning?

options.why: Bio means life, but bi means two.
Manual comes from manus, meaning hand. Mango does not.
Dict means say, and dino means terrible.

hints: Two words can start with the same letters but have different roots.
Work out the meaning of each part, then compare.
Start with portable. What does port mean, and is it in the other word with the same meaning?
items.explanation: Portable (able to be carried) and transport (carry across) both contain port, meaning carry. The other pairs only look alike.

items.prompt: The Latin root port means carry. Which word means easy to carry?
hints: Think about what the word must mean if port means carry.
Add -able, which means can be done.
Port plus able: can be carried.
items.explanation: Portable is port (carry) plus -able (can be). So it means able to be carried.

options.why: Portion means a part of something. It does not come from the root meaning carry.
A portrait is a picture of a person. It is not about carrying.
A porch is an entrance to a house. It has nothing to do with carrying.

items.prompt: Match each Latin root to its meaning.
hints: Think of a word you know with each root.
Spectator, dictate, transport and construct all use these roots.
Start with spect: a spectator watches.
items.explanation: Spect means look, dict means say, port means carry and struct means build.

items.prompt: The officer will ___ our bags before we get on the plane.
hints: The root spect means look.
Which word means to look closely at something?
Spect hides inside only one of these words.
items.explanation: Inspect means to look at something closely. It comes from in plus spect, look.

items.prompt: Bio means life and logy means the study of. Write the word for the study of living things.
hints: Join the two roots together.
Put bio first, then logy.
Bio + logy = ?
items.explanation: Biology is bio (life) plus logy (study of), so it is the study of life.

items.prompt: Put the cards in order to explain the word photograph.
hints: Photo and graph are both Greek roots.
Photo means light and graph means write.
Start with the word being explained.
items.explanation: Photo means light and graph means write, so a photograph is a picture written with light.

items.prompt: Which word came into English from Japanese?
hints: Each word was borrowed from a different language.
Think about the places where these words are first used.
Tsunami means harbour wave in Japanese.
items.explanation: English has borrowed words from many languages. Tsunami comes from Japanese tsu (harbour) and nami (wave).

options.why: Safari comes from Swahili, a language of East Africa.
Algebra comes from Arabic.
Cookie comes from a Dutch word, koekje.

items.prompt: Trans means across and port means carry. Write the word that means to carry goods across to another place.
hints: Join the prefix and the root.
Trans comes first.
Trans + port = ?
items.explanation: Transport is trans (across) plus port (carry).

items.prompt: Port means carry in import, export and portable. Which word does NOT get its meaning from that root?
hints: Three of these words are about carrying.
Ask what each word means. Which one is not about carrying?
A portion is a share of food.
items.explanation: Portion comes from a different Latin word meaning a part or share. It is not about carrying.

options.why: Import means to carry goods in from another country, so it does use the root.
Transport means to carry across, so it does use the root.
Support began with Latin words meaning to carry from below, so it fits the root too.

items.prompt: Sort the words by the meaning of their root.
hints: Look for the letters spect or dict inside each word.
Dictate means to say words for someone to write.
Start with predict: to say before it happens.
items.explanation: Spect means look, so spectators, inspectors and spectacles all involve looking. Dict means say, as in dictate, predict and verdict.

items.prompt: Complete the table of roots.
hints: Each row needs one missing piece.
Use the example word to work out the root or the meaning.
Biology is the study of life.
items.explanation: Spect means look, bio means life, and ped means foot, as in pedal or pedestrian.

items.prompt: Which word is a blend, made from parts of two other words?
hints: A blend uses only a part of each word.
Check which word is missing letters from its parents.
Breakfast and lunch were squashed together.
items.explanation: Brunch is a blend of br from breakfast and unch from lunch. The other words join whole words.

options.why: Sunshine is a compound word. It uses two whole words, sun and shine.
Football is a compound word. It uses two whole words.
Bedroom is a compound word. It uses two whole words.

items.prompt: Noct means night, carn means meat and vor means eat. What does a nocturnal carnivore do?
hints: Work out the two words one at a time.
Carnivore: carn plus vor. Nocturnal: noct plus a word ending.
Put the two meanings together.
items.explanation: Carnivore means meat eater and nocturnal means active at night, so the animal hunts and eats meat at night.

options.why: A plant eater is a herbivore. Carn means meat.

options.text: Hunts and eats meat at night

options.why: Carn means meat, and nocturnal is about the night.

options.text: Hunts for meat during the day
options.why: Nocturnal is about the night, not the day.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that have a root meaning write.
hints: Look for graph, scrib or script inside the word.
Graph is Greek and scrib or script is Latin. Both mean write.
Check autograph first.
items.explanation: Autograph (graph), describe (scrib) and manuscript (script) all hold a root meaning write.

options.why: Telescope uses tele (far) and scope (look).
Dictionary comes from dict, which means say.
Spectacle comes from spect, which means look.

items.prompt: Choose all the English words that came from Malay.
hints: Think about animals and clothes from Southeast Asia.
Cross out the words you know are from Japan or India.
Three words are left once you do that.
items.explanation: Orangutan, sarong and cockatoo all came from Malay. Karaoke and tsunami are Japanese and pyjamas is from Hindi and Urdu.

options.why: Karaoke comes from Japanese.
Tsunami comes from Japanese.
Pyjamas comes from a word used in Hindi and Urdu.

items.prompt: Un means not, pre means before, dict means say and able means can be. What does the word unpredictable mean?
hints: Take the word apart: un, pre, dict, able.
Translate each piece, starting from the end.
Not + before + say + can be.
items.explanation: Unpredictable is un (not) plus predict (say before) plus able (can be), so it cannot be said before it happens.

options.text: Able to be said before it happens
options.why: The prefix un at the start means not.

options.text: Not able to be said after it happens
options.why: Pre means before, not after.

options.text: Not able to be said before it happens

options.why: Un does not mean again here. It means not.

items.prompt: Ornith means bird and logy means the study of. Write the word for the study of birds.
hints: Join the root and the ending.
Ornith comes first and the ending is -ology.
Check the spelling: orn-i-th-ology.
items.explanation: Ornithology is ornith (bird) plus ology (study of).
